title: The hardest part of my game was actually refining player onboarding
author: NSTStudios
selftext:
A few weeks ago I woke up with an idea for a Wordle-style game where the clues are based on the relative order of letters in the word.

After checking that nothing similar existed, I threw together a quick mock-up, super excited that my family was going to love it. The moment they loaded it and started reading the instructions, I realised they had no idea what the game was about. What seemed so clear in my head was apparently impossible to understand.

So I sat down with them and explained it, and then they started getting it. Since then, most of the work hasn’t been the game logic itself, it’s been making it easy to get. We went through a lot of versions. **The best part was with AI, I could do/ redo and try so many different ideas so quickly.**   
  
In the end I replaced the instructions with a short starter puzzle: you make two guesses and the game shows you what the clues mean as you go. Then I started sharing it with friends, watching where they got stuck, and refining, refining, refining. 

And here is the shameless self-promotion. I’m hoping you folks will be another litmus test for whether the game a) makes sense as described, and b) has any replayability. It’s free, runs in the browser, and has no sign-up or ads: [https://liminawordgame.com/?utm\_source=reddit&utm\_medium=social&utm\_content=indiedev](https://liminawordgame.com/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_content=indiedev)

I’d really value this community’s eyes on it:

1. Did the starter puzzle make sense, or did you still feel lost?
2. Is the order diagram helpful or just noise?
3. What made you stop, if you stopped before solving?
4. Anything that feels clunky on your phone?

Happy to answer anything about how it was made. Thanks for reading!

comments.author: shlaifu
comments.body:
I played - the problem is that your design is really bad. why are my previous guesses moved to the bottom. why are the letters in my guess not highlighted in the colors, but on the side. it took me a while to figure out what's going on because the info is supplemented on the side, rather than directly on the letters

  
like... you only had to rebuild wordle, how did you fail at this?

replies.author: NSTStudios
replies.body: Thanks a lot for the comments. Some good stuff here. Will keep refining!
